Subject: Cross-Team Process Improvement Working Group – 1st Meeting

 

Re-send – Please reply to this one and ignore the previous email sent. Sorry

 

Hi all,

Hope you're all coping well with this heat!

We've all been invited to form this cross-team working group to look at process improvements across HR Systems, Payroll and Reward. The aim is to bring us together to share ideas, identify pain points, and explore practical improvements that make life easier for our colleagues.

I've had a look at everyone's calendars today and tried to find a couple of possible times that works for as many people as possible for our first meeting: 

*	Option 1: 20 Jul, 2026 (Mon) 11:00am – 12:00pm
*	Option 2: 7 Sep, 2026 (Mon) 11:00am – 12:00pm

20 July is the earliest date that seems work for everyone and would allow us to get the group up and running before the summer break. However, I appreciate that it’s quite close to the payroll run, and some of us may be busy before heading off on summer holiday.  So, if that isn’t the preferred option, the next date that appears to work for everyone would be 7 Sep.

I'd be grateful if you could let me know which option you would prefer, or if neither works, we can certainly look at some alternatives.

For our first meeting, maybe we could simply get together, and agree how we'd like the group to work. As we're representing our respective teams, it would also be helpful if we could each spend a little time beforehand gathering any thoughts, ideas, or challenges from our colleagues. That should give us a good starting point for identifying opportunities to improve our processes together.

I look forward to hearing your thoughts and to working with you all. Many thanks.

Best regards, 

Otter

 

Otter Ho
Total Reward Specialist

People Department|University of Oxford

otter.ho@admin.ox.ac.uk <mailto:otter.ho@admin.ox.ac.uk>

entries.subject: 2024 non clinical uplift_Incremental bar changes for Grade 2
entries.body:
Hi both,

 

Would either of you recall any decisions or have any documentation relating to the Grade 2 increment bar changes made when the 2024 non-clinical pay uplift was implemented?

 

Tracy has asked whether any employees were manually moved onto Spines 7/8 as part of this work. She can’t recall the specific actions that were taken, but has since identified some employees who appear not to have received their expected increment. The bar change implementation was input after the system job to increment so wouldn’t have occurred automatically.  

 

I’ve been unable to locate any documentation specifically relating to the decisions around the Grade 2 uplift/incremental bar changes.

 

I have, however, found a RIG produced by Nik covering the changes he made when implementing the non-clinical uplift in 2024. This does include the changes made to the Grade 2 bar points in the system.

 

I’ve also found a data load file used to move a batch of employees onto Grade 2.6, covering both S and F instances, effective from August 2024. However, I haven’t been able to find any corresponding data load files or documentation relating to Spines 7/8 within that folder. I’ve also reviewed the available change information but can’t see any reference to employees being manually moved onto those spines.

 

This would suggest that no separate data load was undertaken for Spines 7/8, although I appreciate that doesn’t necessarily confirm what was done at the time.

 

Do either of you recall anything about this, or have anything saved that might shed some light on the approach taken? I appreciate it’s a long shot given how long ago the changes were made, but I thought it was worth asking.

 

 

 

Best wishes,

Michael

 

Michael O’Sullivan

Senior Functional Analyst

University of Oxford

It’s that time again — I’ve scheduled your 2026 PDR for Friday 18 September, 12:00–1:00pm, replacing our usual 1-to-1 that day.

As we’ve been through the process before, I won’t go into as much detail as last year. Ahead of our meeting, please complete a new PDR form and send it back to me beforehand so I have a chance to review it.

entries.subject: FW: changing to 38 day balance - workgroups for updating
entries.body:
Hello all

 

In Julie’s absence I’m sharing this work group update request from Chemistry. Is this a significant piece of work? Is it planned?

 

Also, if you could review the questions below and start dropping responses, I will either collate if completed before I go on leave, or Julie can hopefully pick up next week.

 

Best wishes

 

Marie

 

From: Jenna Boyce <jenna.boyce@chem.ox.ac.uk> 
Sent: 26 August 2026 16:23
To: Marie Cooksey <marie.cooksey@admin.ox.ac.uk>; Julie Hickman <julie.hickman@admin.ox.ac.uk>
Subject: changing to 38 day balance - workgroups for updating 

 

Hi Marie/Julie, 

 

Please find attached list of workgroups which will require updating as we move to the 38 day balance. Should any additional workgroups get added over the next month, these will also need to be added. I recommend we agree a cut-off for this information when we have our call in a couple of weeks. 

 

In preparation, please see below some additional questions on which we would appreciate your input. 

 

*	When adding new balances, does leave need to be physically rebooked or just re-saved?

*	Recording any manual adjustments, eg: carried forward, HEI long service

	*	Does this include length of service or already factored into the system? I believe it is already factored, however, want to confirm. 

 

*	If someone carries over leave and leaves within first 3 months (genuinely cannot take their leave), will the system factor this balance into their remaining balance?

*	Can we add additional approvers to the workgroups during this set up? We want to add HR as part of this as a back-up when leave requests get 'stuck'. If yes, Can we assign HR mailbox as an approver or does it have to be someone? 

*	What is a Holiday Scheme? 

*	What is the impact of not having Holiday Scheme attached to the workgroup? 
*	When requesting any new Work Group going forwards, all departments will always need to state which holiday scheme is required (regardless of which arrangement they are following). How do the team do this and is the Holiday Scheme the same as the balance, if not, where do they get this information? 

*	For regrades, new appointments, and similar changes, what is HR Systems’ recommendation for maintaining leave balances, particularly given the requirement under the ERA to retain a record of employees’ leave entitlement? This relates specifically to how manual adjustments should be managed. 

*	Wording is missing from the sentence under point 7 in the 'department considerations' doc: Departments cannot simply update staff records with a new balance. HR Systems. 

*	From Julie’s email “The only scenario where I can see the Dashboard still being required is for a change in hours. I do not think there will always be a difference between the system and the policy, but there are too many potential scenarios for me to provide a definitive answer” Thank you, is it possible to test this to know for sure? 

*	Timeframe of tasks - all tasks completed by HR Systems by 7/10/26 and then HR team to manually add? 

*	How do you manually deactivate the balances on all staff in affected work groups?

*	Can the HR teams assign the grades and do manual carryover and book FC and BHs at the same time? Can HR Systems update holiday scheme on workgroups first? 

*	Clearing pending requests for leavers and historical requests – is there a way to purge requests in the system? 

 

Thanks,

 

Jenna 

 

Jenna Boyce

Deputy Head of Human Resources – Department of Chemistry

Email: Jenna.Boyce@chem.ox.ac.uk <mailto:Jenna.Boyce@chem.ox.ac.uk> 

 

Our HR intranet pages have been updated: HR - Home (sharepoint.com) <https://unioxfordnexus.sharepoint.com/sites/CHEM-HR> 

 



 

This message and any attachments are confidential. You should not copy it or disclose its contents. You may only use the information for the intended purpose. If you have received this email in error, please notify the sender and delete the email immediately
